newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Argos plummets on profit warning.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Argos plummets on profit warning.

text.p: Shares in British store group Argos Plc tumbled on Friday after the catalogue retailer issued a surprise profit warning, which rocked the entire retail sector and added to gloom about Christmas trading.

Argos, heavily geared to the festive season, said additional costs and lower than expected sales meant full year profits were unlikely to exceed the bottom end of market expectations, currently some 140 million pounds ($236.5 million).
Argos's shares immediately lost almost 14 percent of their value and stood 100.5 pence lower at 632.5 pence.

Retail analysts said the company had probably suffered from Christmas sales being weaker than expected as well as tougher competition from a revitalised Woolworths (part of Kingfisher Plc ) and jewellery retailer Signet Group Plc.
"The (profit) forecast was unexpected, but the shares had been underperforming because of fears that the company might have had a challenging December," said one who asked not to be identified.

Argos, one of few retailers to prosper during the lean years of the early 1990s, said sales in furniture, textiles and leisure ranges performed well in the second half, but toys, watches and gifts were less buoyant.
Margins were stronger, but the company said this would not offset lower than expected sales.

"Despite this margin improvement, the effect of lower than expected sales, together with additional operating costs mentioned in the interim report, mean that full year pretax profits are unlikely to exceed the lower end (currently 140 million pounds) of market expectations," the firm said.
Comparable sales growth in the second half was just over six percent, lower than expected.
Argos's warning put the skids under most other retail stocks, as it seemed to confirm fears that Christmas trading was not as joyful for shop owners as some had predicted.
Clothing retailer Next Plc fell at one stage by more than four percent to a five-month low and Kingfisher lost about 2.5 percent.

A mixed December sales survey from Britain's Confederation of British Industry, showing good furniture, carpets, books, grocery sales, but weak clothing, footwear and durable sales, also weighed on the sector. ($1=.5922 Pound)
